correctness.rationale: For all finite projective planes with order \(s\) not divisible by three, counting incidences gives \(BB^{\mathsf T}=B^{\mathsf T}B=sI+J\). In the \(s\equiv2\pmod3\) class, \(v\equiv1\pmod3\) and the spatial adjacency splits into a zero two-space and a complementary space squaring to minus the identity, giving time-order four/eight components and the exact fixed-space exponent \(4\mathbf1_{4\mid t}+4(v-1)\mathbf1_{8\mid t}\). In the \(s\equiv1\pmod3\) class, \(v\equiv0\pmod3\), \(J^2=0\), and \(BB^{\mathsf T}=I+J\). Each spatial eigenvalue \(\pm1\) has one Jordan block of length two and \(v-2\) blocks of length one, lifting to one temporal block of length four and \(v-2\) blocks of length two at each sign. The fixed-space exponent is \((1+\mathbf1_{2\mid t})[\min(4,3^{\nu_3(t)})+(v-2)\min(2,3^{\nu_3(t)})]\), and the exact global operator order is eighteen. Möbius inversion determines all least-period populations. Two separately implemented finite tests agree on projective planes of orders two, four, and five; those tests corroborate rather than replace the unrestricted proof.

originality.rationale: The same projective-plane incidence graphs have a published characteristic-two reversible-wave classification, but that arithmetic yields rank-dependent periods six or twelve. In characteristic three the adjacency and wave Jordan structures differ: for orders congruent to two modulo three the nonconstant graph component squares to minus the identity, while congruence one gives two spatial size-two Jordan chains and temporal size-four blocks. A prior characteristic-three complete-bipartite theorem only involves rank-two adjacency and has maximal clock at most twelve, not eighteen. General second-order reversibility is prior work, not claimed. No inspected or indexed source implies the simultaneous universal 8/18 clock, all-time nullities, and period populations for the stated nondefining-characteristic incidence networks.

value.rationale: Incidence graphs of all finite projective planes are canonical highly structured graph families, and nondefining characteristic is a natural algebraic regime. The exact orbit census reveals a genuine eight-versus-eighteen clock bifurcation as the plane order changes modulo three, with a transition from one fixed state to \(Q^{v-1}\) fixed states. A nilpotent all-ones incidence correction yields temporal length-four Jordan blocks; this is not a routine field substitution into the characteristic-two formula, whose period and binary-rank dependence are different. The exact invariant is motivated by reversible network dynamics and projective incidence structure, with plausible use in finite dynamical classifications, without asserting a larger downstream theorem.
